title: BMA executor lifecycle types
description: Token bootstrap, registration, capabilities, heartbeat and drain.

ExecutorInfo.description: Executor identity reported at token bootstrap and registration.

labels.description: Contract 1.4.0, optional. Labels the executor reports about itself (at most 32, each 1-64 characters of a-z 0-9 . _ -), set by the machine's owner in the executor's local configuration (for example BMA_LABELS or the SDK Options.Labels). The platform accepts them as given and does not validate their meaning, and it adds its own os:<os> and arch:<arch> labels from os and arch. Labels only narrow a choice among machines the project is already authorized to use (environment placement selectors); no authorization or security decision depends on them. Omitted: no labels.

secret_env.description: The executor accepts transport.secret_env on stdio servers: resolved secret values it injects only into the server process environment, never persisting, logging or echoing them. Without it the server keeps secret: references in env, which the executor rejects.

DisplayCapability.description: v1.1 display object. v1 sent a boolean; the server accepts both.

desktop.description: The machine runs its own desktop (bmad supervises bma-desktop-session from machine start) and serves desktop.attach. Absent means unknown (an executor that predates the field).

native_webrtc.description: Deprecated (screen_live replaces it; removed once no executor declares it). Native screen producer supports screen.start/stop and the bma desktop relay, without process execution. Does not grant input authority.

screen_live.description: The executor's screen publisher serves screen.live: it publishes the machine's screen into the SFU (a desktop, or a physical screen such as a phone's). Not together with native_webrtc.

screen_control.description: With screen_live: the executor serves screen.control and admits a lease holder's signed input (desktop-relay.md §5b).

ProcessCapability.description: v1.1 process.* support. pty, file_transfer, package_install and git_credentials are additive: the harness only sends the matching process.start fields to an executor that set them, and fails the process explicitly otherwise.

ArtifactCapability.description: v1.1 artifact upload (POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/artifacts; legacy alias POST /v1/executors/artifacts). Environment-scoped executors only.

TerminalCapability.description: v1.1 terminal.* support. Machine-scoped executors only.

WorkspaceCapability.description: workspace.backup support and the startup restore of a pending backup. Machine-scoped executors only.

SessionFilesCapability.description: Executor-owned per-session file layout. The harness derives <root>/<agent_session_id>/uploads (read-only session inputs) and <root>/<agent_session_id>/outputs (deliverables) from it, with agent_session_id as sent in process.start metadata, and uses these real paths in prompts, tool descriptions, write rules and the session files manifest. Absent: the executor has no session files; the harness names no session path to it. There is no fixed /mnt/session/uploads or /mnt/session/outputs layout: the per-session <root>/<agent_session_id>/{uploads,outputs} is the only one, and platform-hosted machines declare root /mnt/session. Fixed at executor.register: executor.capabilities.update does not change it. Machine-scoped executors only.

root.description: Absolute, already-expanded, clean path on the executor host (no ~, no . or .. segments, no trailing /).

memory.description: Contract 2.6.0. The executor materializes the session's memory stores: before every process.start of an agent session and on session_files.sync it mirrors the memory_stores of the session files manifest into <root>/<agent_session_id>/memory/<slug>/ (files 0444, platform wins, anything not in the manifest removed, marker <root>/<agent_session_id>/memory/.bma-memory.json) and exports BMA_MEMORY_DIR=<root>/<agent_session_id>/memory to that session's processes. Absent or false: the platform sends no session_files.sync, records one non-terminal session.error memory_unsupported per turn of a session with memory stores, and tells the model memory is not available there.

mount.description: Contract 2.7.0 (ADR-0111). The executor mounts the session's uploads and memory stores instead of copying them: at the points it would copy (before every process.start of an agent session, on session_files.sync) it serves <root>/<agent_session_id>/uploads as one read-only file system and each memory store <root>/<agent_session_id>/memory/<slug> as its own (read-only for access read_only), with the same paths, manifest, content routes and marker as the copy. Content is read lazily (Range on the session files content route) and cached by sha256; each mount root belongs to the OS user that session's processes run as (0700) and answers only that user. A declaring executor fails a process start or a sync whose mount fails; it never copies instead. Declared only after the executor's mount probe succeeded; outputs stay a scanned local directory. Absent or false: the copy protocol.

memory_writeback.description: Contract 2.8.0 (requires memory). The executor writes back the session's read_write memory stores (ADR-0110): a file created, changed or deleted under <root>/<agent_session_id>/memory/<slug>/ is sent to the platform against the content_sha256 it materialized (PUT/DELETE …/session/memory/{memory_store_id}/memories?path=) on the 2 s walk (after two equal observations), when a process of the session ends, on session_files.sync, when the session goes idle and at executor shutdown, before the mirror refreshes the directory, each bounded; a session idle for 15 min keeps its bases on the machine, so a change made after (an on-machine brain's own tools in a long turn) is written back at its next refresh; the store wins a conflict; more than 50 deletions of one store in one sync are refused; a missing marker or unknown base resets the store's directory; reports are delivered in session_memory. read_only stores and read_write stores are both mirrored; only read_write files are written 0644. A writeback failure never fails a process, sync or turn. Absent or false: memory is read-only on this executor and the platform refuses file-tool writes into it.

SessionFilesStats.description: Contract 2.7.0 (ADR-0111). Cumulative session files counters of this executor process (reset when it restarts), reported with executor.heartbeat by an executor that mounts or tried to mount session files. The platform exports them as metrics; it does not act on them.

mount_unavailable.description: Why the mount probe failed (session_files.mount is then not declared and the machine copies); absent when the probe succeeded.

mount_failures.description: Mounts that failed (each failed a process start or a sync).

reads_cached.description: File opens served from the content cache.

reads_fetched.description: File opens that fetched content from the platform.

fetch_errors.description: Content fetches that failed (the read answered EIO).

commits.description: Memory writes committed to the store.

conflicts.description: Memory writes the store refused as a conflict.

commit_failures.description: Memory writes refused or not saved for any other reason.

RemoteBrainCapability.description: Contract 1.4.0. The machine's owner allows a brain that runs on another machine to use this machine as its hands (platform tools routed here for a session whose brain machine is a different one). Set only by the executor's local configuration (bmad configuration or SDK Options.RemoteBrain); the platform reads it back and cannot switch it on through any API. Absent or enabled=false: off, which is also what an executor that predates 1.4.0 means. It applies to a BYO (tenant-owned) machine; a platform pool machine does not need it. It does not restrict a platform-hosted brain driving this machine (project authorization is enough there), and a brain and hands on one machine never need it.

EgressCapability.description: Contract 1.9.0. The executor runs the local egress forwarder (docs/architecture/env-networking-egress.md E6): a loopback HTTP proxy that the processes and terminals of a session are pointed at (HTTP(S)_PROXY, NO_PROXY and a trust store that includes the handoff's ca_bundle), and that tunnels each of their connections to executor.<domain>/v1/machines/{machine_id}/egress?host=<host>&port=<port> (WebSocket, Authorization: Bearer <the session's egress token>). The platform hands an egress handoff (EgressHandoff, session.assign and turn.start metadata egress) only to an executor that declared forwarder=true; a session that needs egress (limited networking or vault environment variables) on an executor that did not declare it is never run there: its turn ends with session.error bma_error_code egress_unsupported (fail closed). Machine-scoped executors only. Absent or forwarder=false: no forwarder, which is also what an executor that predates 1.9.0 means.

EgressHandoff.description: Contract 1.9.0. The egress of one session, carried as the JSON text of metadata egress (session.assign, turn.start). token is secret material: the executor keeps it in memory for the forwarder only, never puts it in a process environment, a log, a session.event or a tool result, and never uses one session's token for another session's connections (several sessions may share the machine). env maps a vault environment variable name to its placeholder: the executor sets these variables in the processes and terminals it starts for the session; the gateway replaces a placeholder with the secret only on hosts the credential allows, so the plaintext never reaches the machine. A refused host is not a protocol error: the forwarder answers the client with the gateway's HTTP status and body (403 naming the host; 401 expired or unknown token; 404 machine is not the token's; 502 unreachable).

ca_bundle.description: PEM of the egress CA (the gateway terminates TLS only on hosts with a credential to substitute).

Capabilities.description: Executor capability object. The server only sends a method to an executor that advertised its capability; otherwise the executor answers -32012 capability_unavailable.

display.description: v1 boolean or v1.1 DisplayCapability object.

ExecutorRegisterResult.description: executor.register result. protocol and limits are v1.1 only.

ExecutorTokenRefreshResult.description: executor.token.refresh result: the connection now closes with 4001 at expires_at.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 time of the new connection deadline.

ExecutorTokenRequest.description: Token request body for POST /v1/machines/{machine_id}/token (bearer: machine daemon token) and POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/token (bearer: environment key); the legacy aliases take one bearer each: POST /api/v1/executors/token a machine daemon token, POST /v1/executors/token an environment key (the other kind is answered 401). The id in the path must equal the credential's machine or environment, otherwise 404; on the new paths environment_id may be empty or absent for a machine and, when sent for an environment, must equal the path id. An empty environment_id with a machine token requests a machine-scoped executor: its executor_id is exec_<machine_id>, stable across refreshes, and the JWT carries machine_id and daemon_token_id.

instance_id.description: Contract 1.23.0, optional (ADR-0083). One instance of a platform brain fleet: the instances of a platform brain machine share its machine credential, and each exchanges it for a token of its own instance (for example its pod name), so each holds its own control channel and the platform spreads sessions over them. Only the deployment's platform brain machines may send it (others: 400 invalid_request_error). Omitted: the machine's own executor.

ExecutorTokenResponse.description: Token response of POST /v1/machines/{machine_id}/token, POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/token and the legacy aliases POST /api/v1/executors/token and POST /v1/executors/token.

token.description: Short-lived executor JWT, sent only in the Authorization header of the channel upgrade.

ScreenLiveResult.description: accepted: the command took effect. published: true exactly for an accepted screen_live_start (the track is published), false for renew and stop.

projection_retained.description: Confirmed suspended capture after clean viewer detachment. The detached peer does not publish video or accept input.

projection_stopped.description: Confirmed full capture stop or confirmed absence for the exact requested session.

SessionFilesSyncResult.description: session_files.sync result (contract 2.6.0). state synced: the session's memory directory equals the manifest's memory_stores; failed: the mirror could not be completed (error names why) and the platform fails the call or turn with memory_sync_failed.

session_memory.description: On an executor with session_files.memory_writeback. Contract 2.8.0. Memory writeback reports (ADR-0110) the executor has not delivered yet for this session, each delivered once: every path of a read_write memory store whose change did not land as the agent left it. Absent or empty: nothing to report. A writeback that could not reach the platform does not make the result failed: it is retried by the next walk.

SessionFilesFlushResult.description: session_files.flush result. state flushed: every changed output was uploaded; failed: at least one upload failed (error names it) and the request may be repeated.
